en: The Philippines is an archipelago composed of 7,641 islands, according to the latest official count by NAMRIA.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
Luzon is the largest island in the Philippines, covering a land area of roughly 109,965 square kilometers.
Mount Mayon in Albay is the most active volcano in the country, with an elevation of 2,462 meters.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an 8.2-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Philippine Trench is the deepest oceanic trench in the country, reaching a depth of 10,540 meters.
The Philippine Eagle is one of the largest eagles in the world, featuring a wingspan of up to two meters.
Mount Pulag is the third highest peak in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,928 meters above sea level.
The Philippines is divided into 81 provinces, which are geographically grouped into 17 different administrative regions.
The Philippine Sea is a massive marginal sea east of the archipelago, covering about 5 million square kilometers.
